To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein intake does not need to be high to gain muscle with resistance training, and that variability in protein intake does not appear to affect the amount of muscle gained.

1) protein intake variability did not affect variability in muscle mass changes induced with resistance exercise training (i.e. variability in muscle mass gain was similar between groups with different levels of protein intake), and 2) a post-exercise supplement (0.4g/kg lean mass protein) may be effective in increasing muscle mass in older adults.

1) protein supplementation after each exercise session was associated with increased lean mass in older adults, and 2) variability in daily protein intake did not influence variability in lean mass changes.

protein intake is not a limiting factor for muscle hypertrophy in older adults.

the variability of protein intake in the context of the post-exercise protein consumption is not a major determinant of muscle gain with resistance exercise training.
